Keep every row in order. Preserve all [[I]], [[B]], [[SC]] emphasis markers, [[Nnumber]] note markers and explicit source line counts. Do not return hashes; the host binds immutable hashes.", "context": {"title": "David Copperfield", "unit": 34, "heading": "CHAPTER 32. THE BEGINNING OF A LONG JOURNEY", "previous_rows": [{"source_id": "en85-u034-b0062", "target": "Большой чепец на голове мисс Моучер и ещё больший чепец на стене снова пошли взад и вперёд, когда она задала этот вопрос.", "source_sha256": "42fc0fd633d02aa67549b807394c4af09bd47709313a9a86106c36c08d3f2cca", "target_id": "ru-en85-u034-b0062", "tag": "p", "target_sha256": "ca06c4a2b6bf31fdb458f90cc37fd21c2769b8c1290180d19445c3ce85e0a89a"}, {"source_id": "en85-u034-b0063", "target": "Я очень хорошо помнил, о чём она говорит, поскольку в тот день думал об этом много раз. Я так ей и сказал.", "source_sha256": "be9b4f485500226abd3026b10fcc5051b8913e7a64103ccbead0eb6624e78a51", "target_id": "ru-en85-u034-b0063", "tag": "p", "target_sha256": "2c5b36088bd701aa5157ba25c0b517559b97d680449b70ef0a10afc229dbfc82"}], "source_language": "English", "part": null, "book": null, "chapter": 32, "role": "chapter"}, "source_rows": [{"id": "en85-u034-b0064", "tag": "p", "role": "paragraph", "text": "‘May the Father of all Evil confound him,’ said the little woman, holding up her forefinger between me and her sparkling eyes, ‘and ten times more confound that wicked servant; but I believed it was YOU who had a boyish passion for her!’", "sha256": "4ccf891de19bc6c829820f5845d5441ff0849fc34e13ba35f5a3ee6dd27e0bee", "source_xpath": "/html/body/div[39]/p[64]", "emphasis_spans": 0, "bold_spans": 0, "smallcaps_spans": 0, "note_markers": [], "source_class": ""}, {"id": "en85-u034-b0065", "tag": "p", "role": "paragraph", "text": "‘I?’ I repeated.", "sha256": "2ec440561a3bcb69d55540178affebb5459a225389dee1f5ed1a47f4b1321585", "source_xpath": "/html/body/div[39]/p[65]", "emphasis_spans": 0, "bold_spans": 0, "smallcaps_spans": 0, "note_markers": [], "source_class": ""}, {"id": "en85-u034-b0066", "tag": "p", "role": "paragraph", "text": "‘Child, child! In the name of blind ill-fortune,’ cried Miss Mowcher, wringing her hands impatiently, as she went to and fro again upon the fender, ‘why did you praise her so, and blush, and look disturbed?’", "sha256": "7ff611e6120d3d8be445571b193cd35959d9f8ac66c2178fdf8c4f3446598cdf", "source_xpath": "/html/body/div[39]/p[66]", "emphasis_spans": 0, "bold_spans": 0, "smallcaps_spans": 0, "note_markers": [], "source_class": ""}, {"id": "en85-u034-b0067", "tag": "p", "role": "paragraph", "text": "I could not conceal from myself that I had done this, though for a reason very different from her supposition.", "sha256": "aab40a88d49e32b53518418a15506d072cdeecced761f362bd5aec227eee1c60", "source_xpath": "/html/body/div[39]/p[67]", "emphasis_spans": 0, "bold_spans": 0, "smallcaps_spans": 0, "note_markers": [], "source_class": ""}, {"id": "en85-u034-b0068", "tag": "p", "role": "paragraph", "text": "‘What did I know?’ said Miss Mowcher, taking out her handkerchief again, and giving one little stamp on the ground whenever, at short intervals, she applied it to her eyes with both hands at once. ‘He was crossing you and wheedling you, I saw; and you were soft wax in his hands, I saw. Had I left the room a minute, when his man told me that “Young Innocence” (so he called you, and you may call him “Old Guilt” all the days of your life) had set his heart upon her, and she was giddy and liked him, but his master was resolved that no harm should come of it—more for your sake than for hers—and that that was their business here? How could I BUT believe him? I saw Steerforth soothe and please you by his praise of her! You were the first to mention her name. You owned to an old admiration of her. You were hot and cold, and red and white, all at once when I spoke to you of her. What could I think—what DID I think—but that you were a young libertine in everything but experience, and had fallen into hands that had experience enough, and could manage you (having the fancy) for your own good? Oh! oh! oh! They were afraid of my finding out the truth,’ exclaimed Miss Mowcher, getting off the fender, and trotting up and down the kitchen with her two short arms distressfully lifted up, ‘because I am a sharp little thing—I need be, to get through the world at all!—and they deceived me altogether, and I gave the poor unfortunate girl a letter, which I fully believe was the beginning of her ever speaking to Littimer, who was left behind on purpose!’", "sha256": "1120b5506bbd5448bd7f819213a751fc939ee8ab310601ff6f4d883271462837", "source_xpath": "/html/body/div[39]/p[68]", "emphasis_spans": 0, "bold_spans": 0, "smallcaps_spans": 0, "note_markers": [], "source_class": ""}, {"id": "en85-u034-b0069", "tag": "p", "role": "paragraph", "text": "I stood amazed at the revelation of all this perfidy, looking at Miss Mowcher as she walked up and down the kitchen until she was out of breath: when she sat upon the fender again, and, drying her face with her handkerchief, shook her head for a long time, without otherwise moving, and without breaking silence.", "sha256": "bb9cf43a6276b5bcce783b9d4ea4b5f897696d2c0bd537ff434ed5ef1c44c17d", "source_xpath": "/html/body/div[39]/p[69]", "emphasis_spans": 0, "bold_spans": 0, "smallcaps_spans": 0, "note_markers": [], "source_class": ""}, {"id": "en85-u034-b0070", "tag": "p", "role": "paragraph", "text": "‘My country rounds,’ she added at length, ‘brought me to Norwich, Mr. Copperfield, the night before last. What I happened to find there, about their secret way of coming and going, without you—which was strange—led to my suspecting something wrong. I got into the coach from London last night, as it came through Norwich, and was here this morning. Oh, oh, oh! too late!’", "sha256": "53f0cdd660b09dfe8b41c1888bd0f8ca9d253cd66dd709eceba1db6e9a0bbf4e", "source_xpath": "/html/body/div[39]/p[70]", "emphasis_spans": 0, "bold_spans": 0, "smallcaps_spans": 0, "note_markers": [], "source_class": ""}, {"id": "en85-u034-b0071", "tag": "p", "role": "paragraph", "text": "Poor little Mowcher turned so chilly after all her crying and fretting, that she turned round on the fender, putting her poor little wet feet in among the ashes to warm them, and sat looking at the fire, like a large doll. I sat in a chair on the other side of the hearth, lost in unhappy reflections, and looking at the fire too, and sometimes at her.", "sha256": "d8232db86ae255c75e3253efe9b912e11fd31b34890ed48df61d18427a545451", "source_xpath": "/html/body/div[39]/p[71]", "emphasis_spans": 0, "bold_spans": 0, "smallcaps_spans": 0, "note_markers": [], "source_class": ""}, {"id": "en85-u034-b0072", "tag": "p", "role": "paragraph", "text": "‘I must go,’ she said at last, rising as she spoke. ‘It’s late. You don’t mistrust me?’", "sha256": "bf7de3f5c5a96800fa2708a492cc1a10c0607202e62ef6be4b421003b50b302b", "source_xpath": "/html/body/div[39]/p[72]", "emphasis_spans": 0, "bold_spans": 0, "smallcaps_spans": 0, "note_markers": [], "source_class": ""}, {"id": "en85-u034-b0073", "tag": "p", "role": "paragraph", "text": "Meeting her sharp glance, which was as sharp as ever when she asked me, I could not on that short challenge answer no, quite frankly.", "sha256": "9eeefd1682be594156a720db127ddd0d99c9c0ec109590821d35dd5ed27aaebe", "source_xpath": "/html/body/div[39]/p[73]", "emphasis_spans": 0, "bold_spans": 0, "smallcaps_spans": 0, "note_markers": [], "source_class": ""}, {"id": "en85-u034-b0074", "tag": "p", "role": "paragraph", "text": "‘Come!’ said she, accepting the offer of my hand to help her over the fender, and looking wistfully up into my face, ‘you know you wouldn’t mistrust me, if I was a full-sized woman!’", "sha256": "1196cf9a77cd3fc174a749ea5513781b48a1d337d349cb238426a47d74731d66", "source_xpath": "/html/body/div[39]/p[74]", "emphasis_spans": 0, "bold_spans": 0, "smallcaps_spans": 0, "note_markers": [], "source_class": ""}, {"id": "en85-u034-b0075", "tag": "p", "role": "paragraph", "text": "I felt that there was much truth in this; and I felt rather ashamed of myself.", "sha256": "eaa7741497e0fd741f9828e077bf82962f3091e1260fccb704bba9ae4af4ce26", "source_xpath": "/html/body/div[39]/p[75]", "emphasis_spans": 0, "bold_spans": 0, "smallcaps_spans": 0, "note_markers": [], "source_class": ""}, {"id": "en85-u034-b0076", "tag": "p", "role": "paragraph", "text": "‘You are a young man,’ she said, nodding. ‘Take a word of advice, even from three foot nothing. Try not to associate bodily defects with mental, my good friend, except for a solid reason.’", "sha256": "ab3c2947492b132334aaed39cf7b5a03d4207b33b445535e168898c6b46b5a3c", "source_xpath": "/html/body/div[39]/p[76]", "emphasis_spans": 0, "bold_spans": 0, "smallcaps_spans": 0, "note_markers": [], "source_class": ""}, {"id": "en85-u034-b0077", "tag": "p", "role": "paragraph", "text": "She had got over the fender now, and I had got over my suspicion. I told her that I believed she had given me a faithful account of herself, and that we had both been hapless instruments in designing hands. She thanked me, and said I was a good fellow.", "sha256": "4c2e1c9a0be47bb9f64140a7e0eaf598714dd1ab4a5a901013d5686ee90bec7b", "source_xpath": "/html/body/div[39]/p[77]", "emphasis_spans": 0, "bold_spans": 0, "smallcaps_spans": 0, "note_markers": [], "source_class": ""}, {"id": "en85-u034-b0078", "tag": "p", "role": "paragraph", "text": "‘Now, mind!’ she exclaimed, turning back on her way to the door, and looking shrewdly at me, with her forefinger up again.—‘I have some reason to suspect, from what I have heard—my ears are always open; I can’t afford to spare what powers I have—that they are gone abroad. But if ever they return, if ever any one of them returns, while I am alive, I am more likely than another, going about as I do, to find it out soon. Whatever I know, you shall know. If ever I can do anything to serve the poor betrayed girl, I will do it faithfully, please Heaven! And Littimer had better have a bloodhound at his back, than little Mowcher!’", "sha256": "af60eef7bcdb5818a058ea8bf18b360378c200de393a18bd1f11066c476cf6d1", "source_xpath": "/html/body/div[39]/p[78]", "emphasis_spans": 0, "bold_spans": 0, "smallcaps_spans": 0, "note_markers": [], "source_class": ""}, {"id": "en85-u034-b0079", "tag": "p", "role": "paragraph", "text": "I placed implicit faith in this last statement, when I marked the look with which it was accompanied.", "sha256": "d762d963fdbcd03f01ff0ac3f1eb6d125d9a5ea2e8e281a9227789875a735162", "source_xpath": "/html/body/div[39]/p[79]", "emphasis_spans": 0, "bold_spans": 0, "smallcaps_spans": 0, "note_markers": [], "source_class": ""}, {"id": "en85-u034-b0080", "tag": "p", "role": "paragraph", "text": "‘Trust me no more, but trust me no less, than you would trust a full-sized woman,’ said the little creature, touching me appealingly on the wrist. ‘If ever you see me again, unlike what I am now, and like what I was when you first saw me, observe what company I am in. Call to mind that I am a very helpless and defenceless little thing. Think of me at home with my brother like myself and sister like myself, when my day’s work is done. Perhaps you won’t, then, be very hard upon me, or surprised if I can be distressed and serious. Good night!’", "sha256": "f79451f146b54f3ab5dffbb03d8afcf6735c162f75358f0861915029195329d0", "source_xpath": "/html/body/div[39]/p[80]", "emphasis_spans": 0, "bold_spans": 0, "smallcaps_spans": 0, "note_markers": [], "source_class": ""}, {"id": "en85-u034-b0081", "tag": "p", "role": "paragraph", "text": "I gave Miss Mowcher my hand, with a very different opinion of her from that which I had hitherto entertained, and opened the door to let her out. It was not a trifling business to get the great umbrella up, and properly balanced in her grasp; but at last I successfully accomplished this, and saw it go bobbing down the street through the rain, without the least appearance of having anybody underneath it, except when a heavier fall than usual from some over-charged water-spout sent it toppling over, on one side, and discovered Miss Mowcher struggling violently to get it right. After making one or two sallies to her relief, which were rendered futile by the umbrella’s hopping on again, like an immense bird, before I could reach it, I came in, went to bed, and slept till morning.", "sha256": "598dfc046bc5b5f80639ba312696ecd85b922f26f8de858b67977b750b7437b0", "source_xpath": "/html/body/div[39]/p[81]", "emphasis_spans": 0, "bold_spans": 0, "smallcaps_spans": 0, "note_markers": [], "source_class": ""}, {"id": "en85-u034-b0082", "tag": "p", "role": "paragraph", "text": "In the morning I was joined by Mr. Peggotty and by my old nurse, and we went at an early hour to the coach office, where Mrs. Gummidge and Ham were waiting to take leave of us.", "sha256": "1875ef65d2f8ccf572b494dd0017bc5728b082a735b543417ddd6475900ee222", "source_xpath": "/html/body/div[39]/p[82]", "emphasis_spans": 0, "bold_spans": 0, "smallcaps_spans": 0, "note_markers": [], "source_class": ""}, {"id": "en85-u034-b0083", "tag": "p", "role": "paragraph", "text": "‘Mas’r Davy,’ Ham whispered, drawing me aside, while Mr. Peggotty was stowing his bag among the luggage, ‘his life is quite broke up. He doen’t know wheer he’s going; he doen’t know—what’s afore him; he’s bound upon a voyage that’ll last, on and off, all the rest of his days, take my wured for ‘t, unless he finds what he’s a seeking of. I am sure you’ll be a friend to him, Mas’r Davy?’", "sha256": "011ae5882aaa81df56b3ed0db030ee34705bff94f957f863ea1b58d9af9ed76e", "source_xpath": "/html/body/div[39]/p[83]", "emphasis_spans": 0, "bold_spans": 0, "smallcaps_spans": 0, "note_markers": [], "source_class": ""}, {"id": "en85-u034-b0084", "tag": "p", "role": "paragraph", "text": "‘Trust me, I will indeed,’ said I, shaking hands with Ham earnestly.", "sha256": "2102eda22624e8a2a8a2cc314c3d1c4ee280f8db937a2401a58c1e24e913876a", "source_xpath": "/html/body/div[39]/p[84]", "emphasis_spans": 0, "bold_spans": 0, "smallcaps_spans": 0, "note_markers": [], "source_class": ""}, {"id": "en85-u034-b0085", "tag": "p", "role": "paragraph", "text": "‘Thankee. Thankee, very kind, sir. One thing furder. I’m in good employ, you know, Mas’r Davy, and I han’t no way now of spending what I gets. Money’s of no use to me no more, except to live. If you can lay it out for him, I shall do my work with a better art. Though as to that, sir,’ and he spoke very steadily and mildly, ‘you’re not to think but I shall work at all times, like a man, and act the best that lays in my power!’", "sha256": "47b1bc13b0da31087a002d7564729de551c166bcfebe30cb56b13c6541f05b30", "source_xpath": "/html/body/div[39]/p[85]", "emphasis_spans": 0, "bold_spans": 0, "smallcaps_spans": 0, "note_markers": [], "source_class": ""}, {"id": "en85-u034-b0086", "tag": "p", "role": "paragraph", "text": "I told him I was well convinced of it; and I hinted that I hoped the time might even come, when he would cease to lead the lonely life he naturally contemplated now.", "sha256": "c9d722ad4210cfdea1e786817bb84ef9b466b7fc4a2be8f5ce5eabb6aa836622", "source_xpath": "/html/body/div[39]/p[86]", "emphasis_spans": 0, "bold_spans": 0, "smallcaps_spans": 0, "note_markers": [], "source_class": ""}, {"id": "en85-u034-b0087", "tag": "p", "role": "paragraph", "text": "‘No, sir,’ he said, shaking his head, ‘all that’s past and over with me, sir. No one can never fill the place that’s empty. But you’ll bear in mind about the money, as theer’s at all times some laying by for him?’", "sha256": "3c16e01e007518adee8da0f93654d2145d14b9f43a3fc1c668ad6be31689ea13", "source_xpath": "/html/body/div[39]/p[87]", "emphasis_spans": 0, "bold_spans": 0, "smallcaps_spans": 0, "note_markers": [], "source_class": ""}, {"id": "en85-u034-b0088", "tag": "p", "role": "paragraph", "text": "Reminding him of the fact, that Mr. Peggotty derived a steady, though certainly a very moderate income from the bequest of his late brother-in-law, I promised to do so. We then took leave of each other. I cannot leave him even now, without remembering with a pang, at once his modest fortitude and his great sorrow.", "sha256": "882a103307859360ccf4c1612fac3de98219831c28225c377c5846f8590a091e", "source_xpath": "/html/body/div[39]/p[88]", "emphasis_spans": 0, "bold_spans": 0, "smallcaps_spans": 0, "note_markers": [], "source_class": ""}, {"id": "en85-u034-b0089", "tag": "p", "role": "paragraph", "text": "As to Mrs. Gummidge, if I were to endeavour to describe how she ran down the street by the side of the coach, seeing nothing but Mr. Peggotty on the roof, through the tears she tried to repress, and dashing herself against the people who were coming in the opposite direction, I should enter on a task of some difficulty. Therefore I had better leave her sitting on a baker’s door-step, out of breath, with no shape at all remaining in her bonnet, and one of her shoes off, lying on the pavement at a considerable distance.", "sha256": "e4a41db02c3df9e6c0ab0881c4e6ef4f29ccaf04cc54836f9a07070c08f31205", "source_xpath": "/html/body/div[39]/p[89]", "emphasis_spans": 0, "bold_spans": 0, "smallcaps_spans": 0, "note_markers": [], "source_class": ""}, {"id": "en85-u034-b0090", "tag": "p", "role": "paragraph", "text": "When we got to our journey’s end, our first pursuit was to look about for a little lodging for Peggotty, where her brother could have a bed. We were so fortunate as to find one, of a very clean and cheap description, over a chandler’s shop, only two streets removed from me. When we had engaged this domicile, I bought some cold meat at an eating-house, and took my fellow-travellers home to tea; a proceeding, I regret to state, which did not meet with Mrs. Crupp’s approval, but quite the contrary. I ought to observe, however, in explanation of that lady’s state of mind, that she was much offended by Peggotty’s tucking up her widow’s gown before she had been ten minutes in the place, and setting to work to dust my bedroom. This Mrs. Crupp regarded in the light of a liberty, and a liberty, she said, was a thing she never allowed.", "sha256": "8f0fe77e8870ffa1e244fe608b8f5e174c9196b05f3a48a19a48a5dac7d14e84", "source_xpath": "/html/body/div[39]/p[90]", "emphasis_spans": 0, "bold_spans": 0, "smallcaps_spans": 0, "note_markers": [], "source_class": ""}, {"id": "en85-u034-b0091", "tag": "p", "role": "paragraph", "text": "Mr. Peggotty had made a communication to me on the way to London for which I was not unprepared. It was, that he purposed first seeing Mrs. Steerforth. As I felt bound to assist him in this, and also to mediate between them; with the view of sparing the mother’s feelings as much as possible, I wrote to her that night. I told her as mildly as I could what his wrong was, and what my own share in his injury. I said he was a man in very common life, but of a most gentle and upright character; and that I ventured to express a hope that she would not refuse to see him in his heavy trouble. I mentioned two o’clock in the afternoon as the hour of our coming, and I sent the letter myself by the first coach in the morning.", "sha256": "caf6e67b2cee0904d37d2ee3cfddf5b99498ac8d760286a36472167da4072ad2", "source_xpath": "/html/body/div[39]/p[91]", "emphasis_spans": 0, "bold_spans": 0, "smallcaps_spans": 0, "note_markers": [], "source_class": ""}, {"id": "en85-u034-b0092", "tag": "p", "role": "paragraph", "text": "At the appointed time, we stood at the door—the door of that house where I had been, a few days since, so happy: where my youthful confidence and warmth of heart had been yielded up so freely: which was closed against me henceforth: which was now a waste, a ruin.", "sha256": "a3135fff61f1241924982a2d5ff67d35397757e0108384fc237465bdcb567fd7", "source_xpath": "/html/body/div[39]/p[92]", "emphasis_spans": 0, "bold_spans": 0, "smallcaps_spans": 0, "note_markers": [], "source_class": ""}, {"id": "en85-u034-b0093", "tag": "p", "role": "paragraph", "text": "No Littimer appeared. The pleasanter face which had replaced his, on the occasion of my last visit, answered to our summons, and went before us to the drawing-room. Mrs. Steerforth was sitting there. Rosa Dartle glided, as we went in, from another part of the room and stood behind her chair.", "sha256": "06f4ae9fba5b9062911715ad7df9d88576660581968946956a2498a51f408f81", "source_xpath": "/html/body/div[39]/p[93]", "emphasis_spans": 0, "bold_spans": 0, "smallcaps_spans": 0, "note_markers": [], "source_class": ""}, {"id": "en85-u034-b0094", "tag": "p", "role": "paragraph", "text": "I saw, directly, in his mother’s face, that she knew from himself what he had done. It was very pale; and bore the traces of deeper emotion than my letter alone, weakened by the doubts her fondness would have raised upon it, would have been likely to create.
